siemens.description: Siemens AG (parent) entered DPA; three subsidiaries pleaded guilty to FCPA charges — systematic bribery of government officials in Argentina, Bangladesh, Iraq, Nigeria, Venezuela, and other countries. $800M total penalty (DOJ $448M + SEC $350M). Largest FCPA settlement at time of resolution.

halliburton.description: KBR Inc. (Halliburton subsidiary) pleaded guilty to FCPA violations — $180M in bribes to Nigerian government officials for LNG contracts.

kbr.description: KBR Inc. pleaded guilty to FCPA violations for bribery of Nigerian officials. Halliburton (parent) paid additional $177M.

bae systems.description: BAE Systems plc entered DPA for conspiracy to make payments to government officials in Saudi Arabia, Czech Republic, Hungary, and other countries.

alcoa.description: Alcoa World Alumina LLC pleaded guilty to FCPA violations — $110M in bribes to Bahraini officials through a middleman.

avon products.description: Avon Products Inc. entered DPA for FCPA violations — payments to Chinese government officials.

hewlett-packard.description: Hewlett-Packard enterprise subsidiaries (HP Russia ZAO, ZAO HP, HP Polska sp. z o.o., HP Mexico S. de R.L. de C.V.) pleaded guilty to criminal FCPA charges — bribery of government officials in Russia, Poland, and Mexico. Parent company HP Co. was the entity of record at time of action (pre-2015 split). After the 2015 split, these enterprise operations passed to Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), not HP Inc. (which inherited consumer/printer businesses).

hewlett packard enterprise.description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the successor entity to the enterprise services divisions of Hewlett-Packard Co. that resolved FCPA charges in 2014 (DOJ 14-371). HP enterprise subsidiaries in Russia, Poland, and Mexico pleaded guilty to bribing government officials. HPE was incorporated in 2015 when HP split; it inherited the relevant operations.

jpmorgan chase.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. entered DPA for FCPA violations — 'Sons & Daughters' program hiring relatives of Chinese officials to win investment banking business.

jpmorgan.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. entered DPA for FCPA violations — 'Sons & Daughters' program hiring relatives of Chinese officials.

pfizer.description: Pfizer Inc. entered NPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to health care providers in Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Kazakhstan, Russia, Serbia.

johnson & johnson.description: Johnson & Johnson entered DPA for FCPA violations — payments to public doctors in Greece, Poland, Romania, and to Iraqi officials.

oracle.description: Oracle Corp reached SEC civil settlement (no criminal charges) — Oracle India subsidiary created a slush fund used to bribe Indian government officials to obtain technology contracts. $2M civil penalty.

Oracle Corp reached SEC civil settlement (no criminal charges) — subsidiary employees bribed government officials in Turkey, UAE, and India between 2016-2019 to obtain technology contracts. $23M civil penalty (most recent of two Oracle FCPA enforcement actions).

microsoft.description: Microsoft Corp entered NPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to government officials in Hungary, Saudi Arabia, Thailand, and Turkey.

cognizant.description: Cognizant Technology Solutions Corp entered DPA for FCPA violations — bribery of Indian government officials to obtain construction permits.

qualcomm.description: Qualcomm Incorporated entered NPA for FCPA violations — provided employment and paid internships to relatives of Chinese government officials.

walmart.description: Walmart Inc. entered DPA for FCPA violations — bribery schemes in Mexico, Brazil, China, and India conducted by subsidiaries.

wal-mart.description: Walmart Inc. entered DPA for FCPA violations — bribery in Mexico, Brazil, China, India.

ericsson.description: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson entered DPA for FCPA violations — bribery in Djibouti, China, Vietnam, Indonesia, and Kuwait.

goldman sachs.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. entered DPA (parent company, no admission of guilt); Goldman Sachs (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd (subsidiary) pleaded guilty — 1MDB sovereign wealth fund fraud; ~$1.6B in bribes paid to Malaysian and Abu Dhabi government officials to obtain bond underwriting mandates. $2.9B total penalty (DOJ $2.3B + other regulators). Largest FCPA penalty against a US financial institution.

fresenius.description: Fresenius Medical Care AG entered DPA for FCPA violations — bribery in West Africa, Saudi Arabia, Angola, and other countries.

stryker.description: Stryker Corp entered NPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to government-employed doctors in Argentina, Greece, Mexico, Poland, and Romania.

tyco international.description: Tyco International Ltd. entered DPA for FCPA violations — bribery schemes across 11 countries.

eli lilly.description: Eli Lilly and Company entered NPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to government-employed physicians in Brazil, China, Poland, and Russia.

astrazeneca.description: AstraZeneca Plc. reached FCPA settlement with SEC — improper payments to government doctors in Russia and China.

merck.description: Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. entered NPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to government employees at state-owned hospitals in Russia, Ukraine.

abbott laboratories.description: Abbott Laboratories entered NPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to doctors employed by state-owned hospitals in Greece.

smith & nephew.description: Smith & Nephew plc entered DPA for FCPA violations — payments to Greek government employed surgeons.

baxter international.description: Baxter International Inc. entered NPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to officials in Argentina, Germany, Poland.

biogen.description: Biogen Inc. paid SEC settlement for FCPA violations — improper payments to government doctors in Germany.

general electric.description: General Electric Co. entered NPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to Iraqi government officials under the Oil-for-Food Programme.

ge aerospace.description: General Electric Co. (now GE Aerospace) entered NPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to Iraqi government officials.

airbus.description: Airbus SE entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid bribes through third-party business partners to government officials in Malaysia, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Indonesia, Ghana, and other countries to obtain commercial aircraft contracts. $800M US portion of a total ~$4B multi-jurisdictional settlement (DOJ, UK SFO, French PNF). Largest aerospace FCPA settlement in history.

mobile telesystems.description: Mobile TeleSystems PJSC (MTS, Russian telecom with NYSE ADR) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid approximately $420M in bribes to Uzbek government officials (including a relative of the President) through shell companies to obtain telecom licenses. $850M total (DOJ $850M — joint resolution with SEC).

mts pjsc.description: Mobile TeleSystems (MTS) PJSC entered DPA for FCPA violations — $420M in bribes to Uzbek officials. $850M total penalty.

glencore.description: Glencore plc (Swiss–UK commodities company, London-listed) entered guilty plea for FCPA violations — paid more than $100M in bribes to government officials in Nigeria, Cameroon, Ivory Coast, Equatorial Guinea, Brazil, and Venezuela to obtain preferential oil allocation and contracts. $1.1B total US DOJ criminal fine. Also resolved related commodity price manipulation charges ($485M CFTC). Largest natural resource company FCPA case.

vimpelcom.description: VimpelCom Ltd. (now VEON Ltd., Amsterdam-listed telecom with NASDAQ ADR) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid approximately $114M in bribes to Uzbek government officials to obtain telecom licenses and regulatory approvals. $795M total US/Netherlands resolution. Company rebranded as VEON Ltd. in 2017.

veon.description: VEON Ltd. (formerly VimpelCom Ltd.) entered DPA for FCPA violations — $114M in bribes to Uzbek officials for telecom licenses. $795M US/Netherlands penalty.

alstom.description: Alstom SA subsidiaries pleaded guilty to FCPA charges — systematic bribery of government officials in Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, the Bahamas, and Taiwan to obtain power plant and transportation contracts worth more than $4B. $772M DOJ criminal fine, the largest FCPA criminal penalty at time of resolution. GE later acquired Alstom's power business (2015).

teva pharmaceutical.description: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd. (Israel-based, NYSE-listed) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid approximately $65M in bribes to government officials in Russia, Ukraine, and Mexico to increase pharmaceutical sales. $519M total (DOJ $283M + SEC $236M).

teva.description: Teva Pharmaceutical (NYSE: TEVA) entered DPA for FCPA violations — $65M in bribes to government officials in Russia, Ukraine, Mexico. $519M total penalty.

societe generale.description: Société Générale SA (French bank, NYSE ADR) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid more than $90M in bribes to Libyan government officials through an intermediary to secure investments from Libya's sovereign wealth funds. $585M total US resolution (DOJ $292.5M + SEC $275.1M).

soci\u00e9t\u00e9 g\u00e9n\u00e9rale.description: Société Générale SA entered DPA for FCPA violations — bribes to Libyan sovereign wealth fund officials. $585M total US resolution.

braskem.description: Braskem S.A. (Brazilian petrochemical company, NYSE-listed) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid approximately $250M in bribes to Brazilian government officials and Petrobras executives as part of the 'Lava Jato' (Car Wash) scandal to obtain contracts and preferential pricing. $957M total US/Brazil/Switzerland resolution.

keppel offshore.description: Keppel Offshore & Marine Ltd. (Singapore-listed, Keppel Corp subsidiary) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid approximately $55M in bribes to Brazilian government officials including Petrobras executives to obtain offshore drilling contracts. $422M total US/Brazil/Singapore resolution.

keppel.description: Keppel Corp / Keppel Offshore & Marine entered DPA for FCPA violations — $55M in bribes to Petrobras officials. $422M total penalty.

och-ziff.description: Och-Ziff Capital Management Group (now Blue Owl Capital, NYSE-listed hedge fund) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid more than $100M in bribes to government officials in Libya, Chad, Niger, Guinea, and Senegal to obtain sovereign wealth fund investments. $412M total (DOJ $213M + SEC $199M). First US hedge fund charged under FCPA.

blue owl.description: Blue Owl Capital Inc. (formerly Och-Ziff Capital Management) — predecessor Och-Ziff entered FCPA DPA for $412M for bribing African sovereign wealth fund officials; first hedge fund FCPA case.

total sa.description: Total S.A. (French integrated oil company, NYSE ADR) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid approximately $60M in bribes to an intermediary connected to the Supreme Leader's office in Iran to obtain rights to develop oil fields (South Pars LNG project). $398M total (DOJ $245M + SEC $153M).

totalenergies.description: TotalEnergies SE (formerly Total S.A., NYSE ADR) entered DPA for FCPA violations — $60M in bribes to Iranian officials for South Pars oil field rights. $398M total (DOJ $245M + SEC $153M).

technip.description: Technip S.A. (French engineering, now TechnipFMC, NYSE-listed) entered DPA for FCPA violations — as part of the TSKJ consortium with Halliburton/KBR, Snamprogetti, and JGC, paid approximately $132M in bribes to Nigerian government officials for Bonny Island LNG plant contracts. $338M total (DOJ $240M + SEC $98M).

technipfmc.description: TechnipFMC plc (successor to Technip S.A., NYSE/Euronext-listed) — Technip entered DPA for FCPA violations for Nigeria LNG bribery (TSKJ consortium). $338M total penalty.

snamprogetti.description: Snamprogetti Netherlands BV (ENI subsidiary) entered DPA for FCPA violations — as part of the TSKJ consortium, paid ~$132M in bribes to Nigerian government officials for LNG plant contracts. $365M total ENI/Snamprogetti US penalty.

eni.description: ENI S.p.A. (Italian state-controlled oil major, NYSE ADR) via Snamprogetti subsidiary entered DPA for FCPA violations — part of TSKJ Nigeria LNG bribery scheme. $365M total penalty.

rolls-royce.description: Rolls-Royce plc (UK aerospace/defense, London-listed) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid bribes to government officials in Thailand, Indonesia, India, Russia, Nigeria, China, and Iraq through intermediaries to obtain defense and energy contracts. $170M US DOJ portion of a total ~$800M multi-jurisdictional settlement (DOJ $170M + UK SFO £497M + Brazil $25M). NOTE: Separate from Rolls-Royce automotive (luxury cars).

weatherford.description: Weatherford International Ltd. (oilfield services) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid bribes to government officials in Angola, Algeria, Congo, Iraq, Libya, and Kuwait to obtain oilfield services contracts. $253M total (DOJ $153M + SEC $100M).

weatherford international.description: Weatherford International — DPA for FCPA violations, bribes in Angola, Algeria, Congo, Iraq, Libya, Kuwait. $253M total.

panasonic.description: Panasonic Avionics Corporation (US subsidiary of Panasonic Corporation, Japan) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid bribes to government officials at state-owned airlines and used inflated consulting contracts to obtain in-flight entertainment contracts. $280M total (DOJ $137M + SEC $143M).

embraer.description: Embraer S.A. (Brazilian aircraft manufacturer, NYSE-listed) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid bribes to government officials in Dominican Republic, Saudi Arabia, Mozambique, and India to obtain aircraft sales. $206M total (DOJ $107M + SEC $98M).

daimler.description: Daimler AG (German automotive, NYSE ADR, now Mercedes-Benz Group) entered DPA for FCPA violations — systematic bribery of government officials in 22 countries including Russia, Croatia, Hungary, Latvia, and others to obtain vehicle contracts. $185M total (DOJ $93.6M + SEC $91.4M).

mercedes-benz.description: Mercedes-Benz Group AG (formerly Daimler AG, NYSE ADR) entered DPA for FCPA violations — systematic bribery across 22 countries. $185M total penalty.

alcatel-lucent.description: Alcatel-Lucent S.A. (French telecom equipment company, acquired by Nokia 2016) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid more than $130M in bribes to government officials in Honduras, Malaysia, Taiwan, and Costa Rica through consultants to obtain telecom contracts. $137M total (DOJ $45M + SEC $92M).

nokia.description: Nokia Corporation (NYSE-listed, Finnish telecom) is successor to Alcatel-Lucent's FCPA DPA via its 2016 acquisition. Alcatel-Lucent paid $130M+ in bribes to officials in Honduras, Malaysia, Taiwan, and Costa Rica. $137M total penalty.

abb.description: ABB Ltd. (Swiss–Swedish industrial conglomerate, NYSE-listed) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid bribes to officials at state-owned utilities in Mexico, Honduras, Bangladesh, and Angola. $58.3M total (DOJ $19.1M + SEC $39.2M).

ABB Ltd. second FCPA DPA (recidivist — violated terms of 2010 DPA) — paid bribes to officials at state-owned utility Eskom in South Africa and to officials in Mozambique and Brazil for power infrastructure contracts. $315M total US/Brazil/South Africa resolution. ABB is a recidivist: two FCPA cases totalling $373M.

abb ltd.description: ABB Ltd first FCPA DPA — bribes to utility officials in Mexico, Honduras, Bangladesh, Angola. $58.3M.
ABB Ltd second FCPA DPA (recidivist) — bribes to South Africa Eskom, Mozambique, Brazil. $315M.

sap.description: SAP SE (German enterprise software, NYSE-listed) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid bribes to government officials in South Africa (SOEs: Transnet, Eskom, Prasa), Indonesia, Malawi, Tanzania, Ghana, Kenya, and Azerbaijan to obtain government software contracts. $220M total (DOJ $118M + SEC $102M). Largest FCPA case against an enterprise software company.

sap se.description: SAP SE entered DPA for FCPA violations — bribes to government officials in South Africa, Indonesia, and five other countries for software contracts. $220M total penalty.

rio tinto.description: Rio Tinto plc (UK/Australian mining company, NYSE ADR) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid approximately $10.5M to a consultant connected to a Guinean government official to obtain an iron ore mining license (Simandou project). $98M total (DOJ $30M + SEC $68M).

panalpina.description: Panalpina World Transport (Swiss logistics, acquired by DSV in 2019) entered DPA for FCPA violations — provided corrupt customs clearance payments across Nigeria, Russia, Kazakhstan, Brazil, Angola, and Azerbaijan. $82M total (DOJ $70.6M + SEC $11.4M).

dsv.description: DSV Panalpina A/S (Danish logistics, Copenhagen-listed) is successor to Panalpina World Transport, which entered DPA for FCPA violations for providing corrupt customs payments in multiple countries. $82M total penalty.

archer-daniels-midland.description: Archer-Daniels-Midland Company (ADM, NYSE-listed agri-food giant) entered DPA for FCPA violations — two ADM subsidiaries made improper payments to Ukrainian government officials to obtain VAT refunds on grain exports. $36.5M total (DOJ $17.8M + SEC $18.7M).

adm.description: ADM (Archer-Daniels-Midland) entered DPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to Ukrainian government officials for VAT refunds. $36.5M total.

sanofi.description: Sanofi SA (French pharmaceutical, NYSE ADR) reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA violations — subsidiaries in Kazakhstan and the Middle East made improper payments to government-employed healthcare providers in Russia. $25.2M civil penalty.

textron.description: Textron Inc. (US aerospace/defense/industrial, NYSE) entered NPA for FCPA violations — Bell Helicopter Textron subsidiary made improper payments to government officials in India, Turkey, Nigeria, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Thailand, Indonesia, Lebanon, and Saudi Arabia to obtain aircraft contracts. $20.1M total (DOJ $10.5M + SEC $9.6M).

diageo.description: Diageo plc (UK spirits company, NYSE ADR) reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA violations — subsidiaries made improper payments to government officials in India, Thailand, and South Korea. $16.4M SEC civil penalty.

bristol-myers squibb.description: Bristol-Myers Squibb Company entered NPA for FCPA violations — subsidiary in China made improper payments to government-employed healthcare providers to increase pharmaceutical sales. $14.75M total (DOJ $5M + SEC $9.75M).

bms.description: Bristol-Myers Squibb (BMS) entered NPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to government healthcare providers in China. $14.75M total.

biomet.description: Biomet Inc. (orthopedic implants, now Zimmer Biomet) entered DPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to government-employed surgeons in Brazil, China, Germany, and Mexico. $22.8M total.
Biomet second DPA (recidivist) — additional FCPA violations in Brazil, Mexico, and China found after the 2012 DPA. $17.4M penalty. Biomet is a recidivist FCPA violator.

zimmer biomet.description: Zimmer Biomet Holdings (successor to Biomet) — first DPA for FCPA violations, improper payments to government surgeons in Brazil, China, Germany, Mexico. $22.8M + 2017 recidivist case $17.4M.

zimmer.description: Zimmer Biomet — successor to Biomet which had FCPA DPA for improper payments to government surgeons. $22.8M (2012) + $17.4M (2017) total.

hess corp.description: Hess Corporation reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA violations — subsidiary made improper payments to Libyan national oil company officials (Sirte Oil Company) to obtain oil exploration concessions. $7.7M SEC civil penalty.

hess corporation.description: Hess Corporation — SEC civil FCPA settlement for improper payments to Libyan state oil company officials. $7.7M.

maxwell technologies.description: Maxwell Technologies Inc. entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid bribes to government officials in China through third-party agents to obtain contracts for high-tech energy storage capacitors. $8M total (DOJ/SEC).

tenaris.description: Tenaris S.A. (steel pipe manufacturer, NYSE-listed, Luxembourg) reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA violations — subsidiary made improper payments to Uzbek government officials to obtain oil country tubular goods contracts. $5.4M SEC civil penalty.

willbros group.description: Willbros Group Inc. (engineering and construction) entered DPA for FCPA violations — subsidiary employees paid bribes to Nigerian government officials and Niger Delta Development Commission officials to obtain pipeline construction contracts. $22.4M total.

vitol.description: Vitol Inc. (US entity of Swiss energy trader) pleaded guilty to FCPA violations — paid bribes to government officials in Brazil, Ecuador, and Mexico (including Petrobras and Pemex officials) to obtain oil trading contracts. $135M total penalty. NOTE: Vitol Group is privately held.

olympus.description: Olympus Latin America Inc. (subsidiary of Olympus Corporation, Japanese medical devices, NYSE ADR) reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA violations — paid improper payments to government-employed physicians in Central and South America to sell medical devices. $22.8M SEC civil penalty.

cobalt international energy.description: Cobalt International Energy, Inc. (offshore oil, NYSE-listed, subsequently bankrupt) reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA allegations — improper allocation of Angola oil blocks to a company connected to Angolan government officials. $148.4M settlement.

magyar telekom.description: Magyar Telekom Plc (majority-owned by Deutsche Telekom AG, NYSE ADR) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid approximately $14M to Macedonian and Montenegrin government officials to prevent new market entrants and obtain regulatory approvals for its telecom operations. $95.4M total (DOJ $59.7M + SEC $35.7M). Deutsche Telekom paid an additional $4.4M as controlling shareholder.

deutsche telekom.description: Deutsche Telekom AG (German telecom, NYSE ADR, T-Mobile US parent) — majority-owned subsidiary Magyar Telekom entered DPA for FCPA violations (bribery in Macedonia and Montenegro). Deutsche Telekom paid $4.4M additional as controlling shareholder; total resolution $95.4M.

pride international.description: Pride International Inc. (offshore drilling, now part of Valaris) entered DPA for FCPA violations — paid improper payments to customs officials in Venezuela, India, Mexico, and Kazakhstan. $56.2M total.

valaris.description: Valaris plc (offshore drilling, NYSE-listed) is successor to Pride International which entered DPA for FCPA violations for improper payments to customs officials in Venezuela, India, Mexico, Kazakhstan. $56.2M total.

orthofix.description: Orthofix International NV (medical devices, NYSE-listed) entered DPA for FCPA violations — subsidiary paid bribes to Mexican Social Security Institute employees to obtain medical device sales. $7.4M total.

comverse.description: Comverse Technology Inc. (telecom equipment, formerly NASDAQ-listed) entered DPA for FCPA violations — subsidiary paid bribes to government telecom officials in multiple countries. $2.8M total.

novartis.description: Novartis AG (Swiss pharmaceutical, NYSE ADR) entered DPA and NPA for FCPA violations — subsidiaries Alcon Pte Ltd and Sandoz Inc. made improper payments to government-employed healthcare providers in Greece, Vietnam, and South Korea to increase pharmaceutical sales. $346M total (DOJ $233M + SEC $112M). Multiple subsidiaries involved across a decade of violations.

novartis ag.description: Novartis AG entered DPA/NPA for FCPA violations — improper payments to government doctors in Greece, Vietnam, South Korea. $346M total.

stericycle.description: Stericycle Inc. (US medical waste management, NASDAQ) entered DPA for FCPA violations — subsidiary employees paid bribes to government officials and private healthcare workers in Brazil, Mexico, and Argentina to retain and expand regulated medical waste contracts. $84M total (DOJ $35M + SEC $49M).

cardinal health.description: Cardinal Health Inc. (US healthcare distributor, NYSE) reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA violations — subsidiary made improper payments to Chinese government officials to obtain pharmaceutical distribution licenses. $34M SEC civil penalty.

diebold.description: Diebold Incorporated (now Diebold Nixdorf, NYSE-listed ATM and election technology) entered NPA for FCPA violations — subsidiaries made improper payments to government officials in Russia, Indonesia, China, and Venezuela. $48.1M total (DOJ $25.2M + SEC $22.9M).

diebold nixdorf.description: Diebold Nixdorf Inc. (formerly Diebold Incorporated) entered NPA for FCPA violations — bribes to government officials in Russia, Indonesia, China, Venezuela. $48.1M total.

medtronic.description: Medtronic plc (Irish-incorporated medical device company, NYSE) reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA violations — subsidiary made improper payments to government-employed physicians in China to increase surgical device sales. $8.2M SEC civil penalty.

noble corporation.description: Noble Corporation (offshore drilling, NYSE) entered DPA for FCPA violations — made improper customs payments in Nigeria, Venezuela, and Mexico. $8.2M total (DOJ $2.6M + SEC $5.6M). Noble was one of several oil services companies in the DOJ 2010 oil services sweep.

universal corporation.description: Universal Corporation (tobacco leaf dealer, NYSE) reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA violations — subsidiary made improper payments to government officials in Thailand, Mozambique, and Malawi. $4.4M SEC civil penalty.

parker hannifin.description: Parker Hannifin Corporation (industrial motion/control, NYSE) reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA violations — subsidiary made improper payments to French government employees and to officials in Germany. $4.5M SEC civil penalty.

utstarcom.description: UTStarcom Inc. (US-China telecom equipment, NASDAQ) entered NPA for FCPA violations — provided all-expenses-paid trips and other benefits to Chinese government officials to obtain telecom contracts. $3M total (DOJ $1.5M + SEC $1.5M).

teradata.description: Teradata Corporation (data analytics, NYSE) reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA violations — subsidiary made improper payments to government employees in Turkey and Thailand to obtain data warehousing contracts. $9.3M SEC civil penalty.

barrick gold.description: Barrick Gold Corporation (Canadian miner, NYSE) reached SEC civil settlement for FCPA violations — Acacia Mining (majority-owned subsidiary) paid approximately $6.2M to government officials in Tanzania to resolve a tax dispute and obtain mining concession benefits. $36.2M SEC civil penalty (primarily disgorgement).

ingersoll rand.description: Ingersoll-Rand Company Ltd. (industrial equipment, NYSE) entered DPA for FCPA violations — subsidiary Hussmann International paid bribes to Iraqi government officials through the UN Oil-for-Food Programme. $13M total (DOJ $6.5M + SEC $6.5M).

ingersoll-rand.description: Ingersoll-Rand (NYSE: IR) entered DPA for FCPA violations — subsidiary bribes to Iraqi officials via UN Oil-for-Food. $13M.
